title: Pontian and Hippolytus (13 August)
hook: a pope and his rival, sent to the same mines, reconciled before dying

segments.voice: Yesterday, Our Lady of the Snows, and a legend of summer snow on a Roman hill. Your line was snow in august.

Two men on opposite sides of a split in the church at Rome. Each with his own followers. Each sure the other has it wrong. Then the empire arrests them both and ships them to the same place: the mines on the island of Sardinia, where prisoners were sent to hard labor. Same dust. Same chains. Same shortage of food and light. Whatever they argued about in Rome is very far away. Today, a pope and his rival, and what happened to the quarrel underground.
screen: `OPPOSITE SIDES OF A SPLIT.` → `ARRESTED, BOTH OF THEM.` → `THE SAME MINES.`

segments.voice: Hippolytus was a priest and a learned writer in Rome, sharp and serious. He clashed with the popes of his day over teaching, and over how gently to treat sinners who wanted to come back. The split went deep enough that a group followed him as their own bishop, against the bishop of Rome. Pontian, later, was that bishop of Rome, the pope. So when the persecution came, the Church in Rome was already divided, and the empire took the leaders of both sides. In the mines, tradition says, two things happened. Pontian stepped down from his office, so the Church in Rome could choose a new pope and not be left without a shepherd. And Hippolytus was reconciled to the Church, and urged his followers to return to unity. Both died there, far from home. Their bodies were brought back to Rome, tradition says, and buried, and the Church keeps them together on the same day, the pope and his old rival. Jesus had said it plainly. In the Douay-Rheims: "go first to be reconciled to thy brother." Not after you win the argument. First. These two came to it late, in chains, and the Church still remembers it as peace. It doesn't remember Hippolytus as the man who split the community. It remembers him, with Pontian, as a martyr who came home.
screen: `A PRIEST WHO SPLIT FROM ROME.` · `BOTH SENT TO SARDINIA.` · `ONE STEPS DOWN, ONE COMES BACK.` · `KEPT TOGETHER ON ONE DAY.` · then, large: `GO FIRST TO BE RECONCILED.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone you've been on the other side from, not your worst enemy, but a coworker, a relative, an old friend after a falling-out. Picture the two of you side by side somewhere neither of you chose, the argument far away, and wonder what you'd say first. If you pray, pray for them by name, and for yourself; if you don't, wish them well, once, and mean it as much as you can.
Hippolytus, the priest who opposed Pope Pontian's church. Sent to the same mines, the two were reconciled there, and are honored together as martyrs.
Your line: reconciled in the mines. Seven days now: Camillus, Sharbel, James, the house at Bethany, Peter Chrysologus, the summer snow, and two rivals at peace. Day one thousand fifteen, done.

howItsDone: Catholics may keep the optional memorial of Saints Pontian and Hippolytus on 13 August, remembering them together as martyrs.

chat.says: Why are a pope and his rival honored together on the same day?
options: They were sent to the same mines; there they made peace, and both died as martyrs.
They were brothers, and the Church likes to honor families of saints together.
Hippolytus became pope right after Pontian, so they share one papal feast.
chat.meaning: In the Sardinian mines, tradition says, Pontian stepped down and Hippolytus was reconciled. Both died there, and the Church keeps them together as martyrs.
